additions.reason: The Rebbe states explicitly 'וְעִקַּר אוֹר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא הַכָּבוֹד' (line 4) — 'the essence of the divine light is the kavod.' This is the definitional bechina statement of the entire Torah. The same equation is restated in line 5: 'אֲזַי מְקַבֵּל אוֹר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, שֶׁהוּא הַכָּבוֹד.' The use of 'עִקַּר... הוּא' is a direct predication of shared essence.
additions.source_quote: וְעִקַּר אוֹר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא הַכָּבוֹד, כִּי כָּל מַה שֶּׁבָּרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ־בָּרוּךְ־הוּא לֹא בָּרָא אֶלָּא לִכְבוֹדוֹ

additions.reason: Line 3 pairs the two terms coordinately: 'מּוֹנֵעַ מִמֶּנּוּ אוֹר וְשֶׁפַע שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.' The Rebbe treats 'אור' and 'שפע' as a hendiadys — two names for the same divine outflow that the shadow blocks. They are not cause-and-effect (one does not produce the other); they are co-referential expressions of the same divine bestowal.
additions.source_quote: מּוֹנֵעַ מִמֶּנּוּ אוֹר וְשֶׁפַע שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ

additions.reason: The Rebbe cites Job 28:12 'הַחָכְמָה מֵאַיִן תִּמָּצֵא' (line 6) and immediately derives: 'הַחֲכָמִים שֶׁהֵם אַיִן' — the wise who ARE ayin. The verse is being used not merely as a proof-text but as a bechina statement: wisdom is found IN/FROM nothingness, meaning wisdom and ayin share the same ontological root. This חכמה = אין equivalence is foundational to Hasidic thought generally (חכמה = אין in Kabbalistic frameworks) and is here explicitly invoked in Torah #172 to explain why the wise cast no shadow.
additions.source_quote: כִּי הַחָכְמָה מֵאַיִן תִּמָּצֵא, וְעַל־כֵּן הַחֲכָמִים שֶׁהֵם אַיִן, זוֹכִים לְכָבוֹד

additions.reason: The existential/practical ayin-state — being utterly nullified and 'not of this world' — is the human expression of the metaphysical ayin-quality that defines chokhmah. Line 5 gives a verse interpretation: 'מְלֹא כָל הָאָרֶץ כְּבוֹדוֹ — הַיְנוּ אִם הוּא מִלֹּא כָל הָאָרֶץ, שֶׁאֵינוֹ כְּלָל מִזֶּה הָעוֹלָם' — the phrase 'filling the earth' is interpreted as 'being nothing from this world.' Line 6 establishes that the חכמים (the wise) achieve this state via ayin. The ביטול/אינו כלל מזה העולם and אין belong to the same domain. Note: the existing dataset edge (id=236, type='eitza') encodes the causal link from this nullification STATE to the reception of light — that is correctly classified as eitza. The present bechina edge encodes the identity of the nullification state WITH ayin — these are two faces of the same thing.
additions.source_quote: הַיְנוּ אִם הוּא מִלֹּא כָל הָאָרֶץ, שֶׁאֵינוֹ כְּלָל מִזֶּה הָעוֹלָם

additions.reason: Line 7 states: 'כְּשֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַרְאֶה פָּנִים שׂוֹחֲקוֹת – חַיִּים וְטוֹבָה לָעוֹלָם'. The dash construction — showing joyful face → life and good — is not a causal sequence but a definitional identity: the joyful face IS the mode of life and good reaching the world. Line 8 confirms with 'הַיְנוּ' (definitional bechina marker): 'אֶת הַחַיִּים וְאֶת הַטּוֹב, אֶת הַמָּוֶת וְכוּ', הַיְנוּ לַפָּנִים שֶׁלָּכֶם.' The 'הַיְנוּ' identifies the two as the same reality.
additions.source_quote: כְּשֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַרְאֶה פָּנִים שׂוֹחֲקוֹת – חַיִּים וְטוֹבָה לָעוֹלָם... הַיְנוּ לַפָּנִים שֶׁלָּכֶם

additions.reason: Line 7: 'וּלְהֵפֶךְ – לְהֵפֶךְ, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם' — the exact mirror of the previous bechina. Line 8 cites 'אֶת הַמָּוֶת וְכוּ'' in the same 'הַיְנוּ לַפָּנִים שֶׁלָּכֶם' formula as the positive case. The Rebbe treats the death/evil side as structurally identical to the life/good side: both ARE the face shown. This is the evil mirror of the פנים שוחקות / חיים וטובה bechina.
additions.source_quote: וּלְהֵפֶךְ – לְהֵפֶךְ, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם... אֶת הַמָּוֶת וְכוּ', הַיְנוּ לַפָּנִים שֶׁלָּכֶם

additions.reason: Line 2 provides the metaphysical definition: 'הַצֵּל הוּא מִדָּבָר גַּשְׁמִי שֶׁעוֹמֵד נֶגֶד דָּבָר רוּחָנִי' — the shadow IS from a physical thing standing opposite a spiritual thing. Line 3 applies this directly to the person: 'הָאָדָם כְּפִי גַּשְׁמִיּוּתוֹ... כֵּן עוֹשֶׂה צֵל בְּעַצְמוֹ.' The measure of physicality = the measure of shadow. Physicality and shadow are two faces of the same blocking-reality: one is the cause in the metaphysical-mechanical sense, but in Torah #172's framework they are treated as equivalent degrees of the same obstacle-phenomenon (not as cause-and-effect in separate domains). The proportional 'כְּפִי... כֵּן' construction signals parallel aspects, not sequential causation.
additions.source_quote: הַצֵּל הוּא מִדָּבָר גַּשְׁמִי שֶׁעוֹמֵד נֶגֶד דָּבָר רוּחָנִי... הָאָדָם כְּפִי גַּשְׁמִיּוּתוֹ וּכְפִי מַעֲשָׂיו, כֵּן עוֹשֶׂה צֵל

additions.reason: Line 1: 'הָאָדָם עַל־יְדֵי מַעֲשָׂיו הָרָעִים עוֹשֶׂה צֵל לְעַצְמוֹ.' Line 3: 'כְּפִי מַעֲשָׂיו, כֵּן עוֹשֶׂה צֵל.' The evil deeds and the shadow they produce are treated in proportional bechina terms throughout: the deeds ARE the shadow, expressed in human-deed form. This complements the גשמיות/צל bechina: physicality is the general principle; evil deeds are its human-moral instantiation. Both are aspects of the shadow-blocking domain.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: Line 1 lists deficiencies as outcomes/results of the shadow, not as bechina-equated concepts. 'כָּל הַחֶסְרוֹנוֹת... הַכֹּל הוּא מִצַּד הָאָדָם עַצְמוֹ' — this is a causal claim (the person's deeds CAUSE the deficiencies via the shadow mechanism), not a bechina statement. The individual items (בנים, פרנסה, בריאות) are merely examples, not bechina-partners.

Line 2 defines the shadow in terms of 'דָּבָר גַּשְׁמִי שֶׁעוֹמֵד נֶגֶד דָּבָר רוּחָנִי (הַיְנוּ דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא דַּק מִמֶּנּוּ)'. The parenthetical 'הַיְנוּ דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא דַּק מִמֶּנּוּ' is a definitional clarification of what 'רוחני' means (that which is finer/subtler), not a bechina equivalence of a named concept. No standalone bechina node is being created here.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: Lines 2 are analogical illustrations of the shadow mechanism, not bechina-equated spiritual concepts. The Rebbe uses them as physical examples to explain the metaphysical principle of גשמיות/צל. They are not named as bechinot of spiritual concepts in this Torah.

Line 5 interprets the verse 'מְלֹא כָל הָאָרֶץ כְּבוֹדוֹ' as referring to a person who is 'not of this world.' This is a verse-interpretation technique (the phrase 'מלא כל הארץ' is being reread as describing the person who is filled/full of the earth = rooted in/for the world vs. the Rebbe's reading = the one who is the earth's 'fullness' meaning nothing left for this world). The interpretation supports the Package 2 bechina (ביטול = אין) rather than creating a new concept called 'מלא כל הארץ'.

Line 7 mentions the tzaddik showing a joyful face. The tzaddik is mentioned as the human parallel to God in showing panim — but the Rebbe does not equate the tzaddik with a new bechina concept here. The tzaddik's joyful face IS the same concept as פנים שוחקות (Package 3) — it is the same phenomenon applied to the tzaddik as to God. No new bechina edge is needed; the tzaddik example is an application of an existing bechina, not the establishment of a new one.
